content.content:
A ref-path entry carries "detail__ref" as its whole class, and the stylesheet's rules select that one name. That is the whole of this decision: the name the entry is marked with, stated once, so that the panel's markup and the panel's stylesheet meet on it instead of each arriving at a name of its own.

The name is on that entry and on nothing else, and it is on every one of them. Where a node's content.ref is a list of repo-relative paths, each path the section shows as an entry carries it — on every value of that form, whatever its content type — because the entry squvoxyr commits to reading as a visible link is the path entry, and every such entry is one of those (squvoxyr). It is not on the block that shows the value, not on the section or its label, not on the content type shown beside the paths, and not on the paths as a group in place of the entries themselves, nor on a path mentioned anywhere else in the panel: the name marks the entry, not the surface it sits in. Read where a reviewer reads it — at the element that shows the path and nothing else — the class list is "detail__ref" and nothing beside it, and an entry carrying a second name, or carrying no name where the paths are entries, is the observation that refutes that sentence.

The stylesheet selects that same one name. Every rule the stylesheet writes to present a ref-path entry is written against "detail__ref", so the class the entry carries is what decides which of the stylesheet's ref-path rules reach it, and no rule reaches that entry through an element, a structural position, a second class or any other name in place of this one. There is no second spelling of the name for the stylesheet to select — not a variant, not a shortened form, not an element-scoped reading of it — because a name its own selection does not read could not be what decides which rules reach the entry, and the markup and the stylesheet would then be two accounts of one entry's case rather than one.

The name is not spelled out of the two names a listed entry carries. "detail__ref" is one class name in full and not "detail__entry" with a modifier or qualifier appended, nor either recorded name with an addition: neither recorded name appears in it, and the two diverge at the word that follows the block prefix they share rather than at a suffix. Nor is it one recorded name nested inside the other's block, and nothing is applied beside it: a ref-path entry carries no "detail__entry", no "detail__entry--inert", no second ref-path name, no further modifier, no data attribute, no element id and no other hook, whether beside this name or in its place. One name, carried whole, is all the entry is marked with.

What sqwusxql records is untouched. The cases its two names denote, and the entries that carry each of them, stay exactly as it recorded them: this decision neither changes, extends, narrows nor restates that mapping, and no entry the pair governs gains or loses a name here (sqwusxql). The ref-path entry is not one of the two cases that pair names — it is not a listed entry at all, but the path entry of the Content section's path form — so the distinction drawn here is between that entry and the entries the pair governs, not a finer distinction inside the pair; and because sqwusxql requires a carrier that needs a finer distinction to state it as its own decision rather than spell a name out of its two, this decision states it here, with a name of its own rather than a qualification of theirs (sqwusxql).

The name is the whole of this decision's commitment, and naming the entry settles nothing about how it looks. No declaration follows from the name and none is fixed here: no colour or colour role, no pointer cursor, no hover marking, no focus indicator, no text decoration, underline or outline, no line thickness, weight, spacing or layout, and no placement of the entry in the block. Which rules beyond this one select for the name, what those rules declare, and what further a rule of theirs selects are the stylesheet's own decisions, each settled where it is owned; whether the rules for the name declare the same thing, different things or nothing at all changes no entry's markup, because a class is the name of a case and not a promise that a declaration follows. Nor does the name change what the entry shows or what activating it does: the text stays the path squvoxyr keeps, and what activates the entry and where it leads remain where they are owned (squvoxyr).
content.rationale:
Two carriers have to reach the same string: the panel's markup, which puts a class on each path entry it shows, and the panel's stylesheet, whose rules select the class an entry carries. squvoxyr commits the entry to reading as a visible link and expressly leaves the class vocabulary to another decision; sqwusxql fixes the vocabulary of the listed entry — the id a relationship section lists — and forbids spelling a further name out of its two, using either of them for a case it does not denote, or multiplying them into a third class or a further modifier. A path in the Content section is not a listed id, so it falls outside that pair, and the name it needs cannot be "detail__entry", cannot be "detail__entry--inert", and cannot be either of them with something appended or nested. Any of those would put the entry into a case the vocabulary never defined and make one name answer two questions at once. sqwusxql's own instruction is that a carrier needing a distinction outside its pair states that as its own decision, so this node exists to state that one name, once, for both carriers to cite.

Stating the name where both carriers can read it is what keeps them from drifting apart. If the markup fixed the string and the stylesheet were written to whatever string the markup chose, the stylesheet would have to name the markup's decision, and a rule that named one string while the entry carried another — or that found the entry by its element or its position rather than by its class — would leave the entry styled by whatever rules happen to fall on it, with the name selecting nothing. Fixing the name here, and saying in the same breath that the stylesheet's rules for the entry select it, means each carrier cites this node and the two meet on one string rather than on a guess.

"detail__ref" as the entry's whole class is the smallest form this distinction can take. It is one name in full, so the class list reads unambiguously as the answer to which entry this is; a paired form — the recorded name with this one beside it, or this one nested in the other's block — would both spell a recorded name onto an entry that is not one of that pair's cases and make the stylesheet's selection depend on which of two names a reader happens to look for, reintroducing exactly the both-cases state sqwusxql excludes. Carrying neither recorded name is the other half of the same point: an entry that is none of the pair's cases must not read as one, and the word in the name is the entry's own rather than an addition to theirs. The name belongs to no entry but the ref-path entry, so the block, the section's frame, the content type and the paths taken as a group stay unmarked, and the paths anywhere else in the panel gain nothing from it.

Stopping at the name is what keeps the appearance decisions decidable. The colour role, the pointer cursor, the hover treatment, the focus outline, the weight and the spacing are declarations a reviewer reads in the rule that carries them, and each belongs to the decision that owns it; written here, they would be restated or contradicted there, and one node would answer two questions. Leaving them open costs nothing, because the name is a place for those rules to be written and the entry's mark is stated independently of any declaration existing for it — an abstention on the rules is a decision about a rule, not about which entry is marked. Nothing here reaches past the name either: the entry's text stays the path squvoxyr keeps, and what activates the entry and where it leads remain where they are owned.
